title: Work Map post-write exact verification dispatch

phases.objective: Allow the governed Work Map writer to dispatch CI and Work Map integration against the exact committed branch head, then fail closed if either checkout or remote branch identity differs.

e2e_journeys.actor: Governed Work Map writer and CI evidence reviewer
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Dispatch exact-head verification after the Work Map writer pushes its governed commit
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Both verification workflows accept the writer inputs, check out the committed SHA, verify local and branch identity, and bind test and deployment evidence to that SHA.
steps: The governed writer dispatches CI with expected_head_sha.
The governed writer dispatches Work Map integration with branch and expected_head_sha.
CI checks out and verifies the expected SHA in every load-bearing job.
The Unit and Integration suite publishes reports under the verified checked-out SHA.
Work Map integration verifies both local checkout identity and the current remote work-branch head.
Any missing, stale, or mismatched identity fails before verification evidence is accepted.
assertions: Writer-supplied workflow_dispatch inputs are explicitly declared.
No verification workflow silently falls back to a different branch head when an exact SHA is supplied.
Push and pull-request execution retain their existing event SHA semantics.
No repository write, protected-ref mutation, provider call, deployment, database action, migration, credential access, or external send is introduced.

phases.objective: Publish typed linkage between the writer run, verification run IDs, and exact committed head across the CI evidence families.
Prove exact identity preservation across reruns, concurrent branch movement, and verification dispatch retries.
This repository CI dispatch correction grants no provider canary authority.
This repository CI dispatch correction grants no Production or deployment authority.
